content:
Ana R.: Quick update: I ran a short head-to-head between the current packer and the wavefront-pack heuristic with prefix cache signals enabled. Results look... mixed.
Mike T.: mixed how? latency up anywhere?
Ana R.: p50 similar, but p95 regressed ~18ms on tail when hit ratio is ~30-40% for long prompts. p99 up ~60ms for a subset of streams.
Leo C.: any idea which part of the path is inflating tail? kernel selection or queueing?
Ana R.: traces point to more variable microbatch sizes and a few extra kernel swaps. Looks like when prefix hits packer greedily merges a hit with short non-hit requests we end up with longer prefill kernels for some batches.
Sara L.: can you paste the config used for the run?
Ana R.: sure — minimal diff from prod, token budgets tuned lower, enabled cache-aware packing: 
```
packing: 
  mode: wavefront-cache-aware
  token_budget_target: 64
  prefer_hits: true
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
queue_policy: 
  idle_timeout_ms: 6
  prefill_adm: true
```
Mike T.: prefer_hits=true is the knob that's suspect. If we prioritize hits too aggressively we might force kernel choices that increase context switching.
Leo C.: perf-bot ran a profile on the same run: 
perf-bot: cpu:kernel-switches +22%, memcpy +12% on tail batches; gpu:launchs slightly higher for certain seqlen ranges.
Ana R.: yeah saw those counters. Hypothesis: hit-preferring merges create heterogenous seqlen groups that defeat the continuous-batching assumptions for kernel selection (we pick a prefill kernel for the long one and then small ones pad it).
Sara L.: what about adding a homogeneity check before merging? only merge hits if estimated seqlen variance < X.
Mike T.: or weight prefer_hits by expected kernel cost: prefer hits *and* (pad_cost_estimate < threshold).
Ana R.: tried a quick patch: require pad_cost_estimate <= 8 tokens and seq_var <= 12, tail median improved 12ms and p99 down ~30ms in the next run. No regressions on p50.
Leo C.: nice. Did you change token_budget_target?
Ana R.: kept 64 for these experiments. When we lowered to 32 overall throughput dropped but latency stabilized. tradeoff.
Mike T.: we should run longer soak across burst workloads. Can you add an ablation matrix for prefer_hits true/false + homogeneity check + token_budget [32,64,96]? I'll spin new canary.
Ana R.: on it. Also adding a synthetic test that simulates 40% prefix-hit long prompts interleaved with 60% short non-hits. That reproduces the worst-case.
Sara L.: also log chosen kernel id per batch into trace so we can correlate kernel-switch churn with p99.
Ana R.: added that to the tracer.
perf-bot: perf alert: previous run flagged 2 regressions; new patch reduces kernel-switch churn by ~15% in the canary window.
Leo C.: next steps: 1) run full ablation matrix 2) evaluate cost impact of smaller token_budget 3) consider adaptive prefer_hits that decays when seqlen variance grows.
Mike T.: agreed. tagging @infra-oncall for a canary window tomorrow. :thumbsup: 
Ana R.: thanks — I'll drop the run artifacts and the ablation CSV in the #eng-runtime dropbox shortly.
Sara L.: SG, thanks Ana.
Mike T.: good work.
